paper_title: Catalytic Aerobic Oxidation of p‑Methoxybenzyl (PMB) Ethers to Aldehydes or Ketones

questions.question: In this paper what does the abbreviation 'PMB' stand for?
questions.ground_truth_answer: PMB = p‑methoxybenzyl (the p‑methoxybenzyl protecting group/aryl‑methylene group)

questions.question: What aryl group (Ar) is used for compound 1a in the paper (how is Ar defined for 1a)?
Under the optimized conditions used to oxidize PMB ether 1a to aldehyde 2a (Table 1, optimized entry), what solvent and temperature were used?
questions.ground_truth_answer: Toluene as solvent and 25 °C reaction temperature (O2 balloon, standard optimized conditions)

questions.question: Comparing entries in Table 1, which solvent (toluene or DCM) gave the higher NMR yield of aldehyde 2a from 1a, and what were the two NMR yields reported?
questions.ground_truth_answer: Toluene gave the higher NMR yield: toluene 71% NMR yield of 2a (entry 4) vs DCM 28% NMR yield of 2a (entry 5)

questions.question: What yield values are reported for aldehyde 2a: the isolated yield shown in Scheme 2 and the NMR yield reported in Table 1 (optimized conditions)?
questions.ground_truth_answer: Isolated yield in Scheme 2: 82% (2a; noted as 2a:4a = 98:2); NMR yield in Table 1 (optimized entry): 71% NMR yield
